meta.title: How to cross the HAI VAN PASS Vietnam 🇻🇳 (Da Nang to Hue)
meta.description:
Crossing the Hai Van Pass Vietnam was one of the best days of my Vietnam trip so far! Riding from Da Nang to Hue, the trip starts off shaky with some torrential rain, luck quickly turned around as the sun came out on the Hai Van Pass and this quickly became one of the best riding days of my life!

The Hai Van Pass Vietnam is a 21km stretch of mountain road that runs between Da Nang and Hue. It's popular for travellers and backpackers to cross the pass on scooters, taking in the breathtaking views from the top. With incredible hairpin turns and much to see, this is a day you don't want to miss when you travel Vietnam!

#haivanpass #vietnam #vietnamtravel #backpacker

comments.author: @slybrookbuster1875
comments.text: 1967-68 I walked up and down both sides of the Hai Van Pass on Road Mine Sweeps.  The Pass back then, was just as beautiful but very deadly.  In October 1967 we took over an ARVN combat base at the next pass on Highway One at north end of Lang Co Bay.  From there we ran mine road sweep north to Phu Loc just south of Phu Bai.  In December 1967 we move to the south side of Hai Van Pass to the Esso Plant and Nam O Bridge on the Da Nang side.  From the south side, we also did the same mine road sweeps to the top of the Pass. We lost people to mines and ambushes on both sides of the Pass.  Back then the railroad bridge in Nam O serviced both the RR, which was not in use and road traffic on Highway One. There used to be a beautiful solid marble turtle monument on the last turn on the north side overlooking Lang Co. The marble tablet on top of the turtle told the story about the longevity and hardship of building the railroad around the Pass. It was all written in French.  I believe that the North Vietnamese Army probably blew it off the turtle when they took over South Vietnam in 1975.  I have seen photos of it without the marble tablet on its back.      Thank you for the memories.  Golf 2/7 Marines, Vietnam.
